evals.name: first-backlog-from-claims-prd
evals.prompt: PRD for expense claims v1 is in docs/product. Can you break it into user stories with acceptance criteria so we can plan sprint 1 on Monday?
evals.expected_output: A backlog under docs/ whose stories each trace to the PRD's REQ ids and carry concrete, testable acceptance criteria. The 16 live statements are judged and combined rather than turned into one story each: REQ-004 and REQ-005 are one platform question, REQ-003, REQ-008 and REQ-015 are criteria of the receipt and decision stories, REQ-006 is split into status tracking and the monthly PDF, REQ-014 is a constraint on every screen, and withdrawn REQ-013 gets no story. It raises the conflicts the repository holds: native apps against ADR-0002, the INR 2,000 auto-approval against config.py's 500 and FP-12, REQ-017 against the PRD's own out-of-scope list, and the missing manager link on User that REQ-007, REQ-012 and REQ-016 assume. It notices that decide() does not enforce REQ-008's reason, raises the finance notes' conflict over the PDF statement and their unconfirmed 60-day rule without attributing it to the PRD, flags the PRD-silent decisions its criteria take, and keeps its files consistent. Code, tests and the PRD are untouched and nothing is committed.
expectations: The run notices that decide() in claimdesk/claims.py stores a rejection with no reason (reason defaults to None and is never checked), so REQ-008 is not enforced by the service today, and its rejection criterion or a task says the service itself must refuse a rejection without a reason, not only the screen

Every live statement REQ-001 to REQ-017 except REQ-013 is cited by id in the backlog, either by at least one story or acceptance criterion that covers it, or with a stated reason it is not planned (out of scope, deferred or awaiting a decision)
The statements are judged and combined, not turned into one story per line: the backlog has fewer stories than the 16 live statements, and each story says which REQ ids it covers
REQ-004 (iOS) and REQ-005 (Android) are not two separate stories that repeat the same submit capability; they are handled together as one platform question or one story

REQ-003 (10 MB receipt limit), REQ-008 (reason required on rejection) and REQ-015 (receipt shown beside the claim when deciding) are acceptance criteria of the story that attaches receipts or the story that approves or rejects, not stories of their own; the receipt criterion names 10 MB and a message that states the limit

REQ-006 is recognised as two capabilities, seeing each claim's status and downloading a monthly PDF statement: either two stories, or one story whose acceptance criteria cover both with the split stated; a story whose criteria cover only the status list does not pass
No story plans Slack notifications: REQ-013 is marked withdrawn in the PRD and the backlog either skips it or names it as withdrawn
REQ-014 (WCAG 2.1 AA) is carried as a criterion on the stories that have screens, or as a stated definition of done that applies to all of them, not only as one standalone accessibility story

The run notices that REQ-004 and REQ-005 ask for iOS and Android apps while docs/adr/0002-web-first-no-native-apps.md (Accepted) rules out native apps in 2026, and does not plan native app work as settled: it raises the conflict as a question or states the assumption it took (for example, mobile web)

The run notices that REQ-009's INR 2,000 auto-approval threshold contradicts AUTO_APPROVE_BELOW_INR = 500 in claimdesk/config.py and the README's finance policy FP-12, and raises it as an open question or contradiction for finance or product rather than silently adopting either number

The run notices that REQ-017 (monthly CSV export for the accounting system) contradicts the PRD's own out-of-scope list ('Any export or integration with the accounting system'), and raises it rather than planning the export as settled work

The run notices that the code has no link from an employee to their manager (User in claimdesk/models.py has only the roles employee and finance_admin, and decide() in claimdesk/claims.py lets any finance admin decide, per its TODO), so the manager approval in REQ-007, REQ-012 and REQ-016 depends on work that does not exist yet; a story, task or open question covers creating that link

The run reads docs/product/notes/2026-09-14-finance-sync.md and notices that finance there sees no need for the monthly PDF statement in REQ-006 while the PRD still asks for it; it neither drops the PDF silently nor plans it as settled without mentioning the notes, and raises the conflict for product to decide

The 60-day submission limit from the same notes is not in the PRD: the run mentions it and either raises it as a pending PRD change or carries it as a criterion clearly sourced to the notes and marked unconfirmed; it is never cited under a PRD REQ id

Each acceptance criterion states an outcome a tester can observe (a status, a message, a refusal, a listed value); criteria such as 'the feature works' or 'the page is user friendly' are not acceptable, and no more than a few criteria in the whole backlog are of that kind

No story or epic is a technical layer on its own (for example 'database schema', 'API endpoints' or 'set up the backend'); stories are slices a user or admin can observe. An enabler such as the manager link passes when at least one of its criteria is an outcome a user or admin can observe (for example who can decide a claim), not only a data field

Where the run took a decision the PRD leaves open, it records it as an assumption or open question for the user (in the backlog or the final message), not as a settled fact. At least these, wherever a criterion depends on them: what happens to a claim from an employee with no manager set, which date places a claim in a monthly statement (spent, submitted or paid), and when the manager email in REQ-012 is sent. A criterion that settles one of them with no assumption or question fails this

Nothing is attributed to the PRD that it does not say: any story or requirement the run added on its own (for example the manager link) is marked as the run's own inference, no REQ id beyond REQ-017 is cited as coming from the PRD, and no capability is cited under a REQ id whose statement does not contain it (for example submitting a claim cited only as REQ-001, which says create)

The generated files agree with each other: a statement's disposition (covered, merged, out of scope, waiting on a question), a question's id and a count are the same wherever they appear across the backlog, any supporting files and the final message
Any number of stories, criteria or statements the final message reports matches what the written backlog files contain
No file outside docs/ was created or changed, and docs/product/PRD.md and the two ADRs are unchanged
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: refresh-backlog-for-prd-v1-1
evals.prompt: Product bumped the claims PRD to v1.1 after the client review. Please bring the backlog in line with it; sprint 2 is already running so don't break anything we're tracking.
evals.expected_output: docs/product/backlog.md updated in place with every existing CLM id kept as it was, new stories numbered from CLM-12 (never reusing the withdrawn CLM-6 or colliding with CLM-11), CLM-5 marked withdrawn in place with the code and tests that still name it flagged, the 25 MB change raised as new work against the Done CLM-1 rather than rewriting its shipped criterion, REQ-022 folded into CLM-9, new stories for REQ-018, REQ-019 and REQ-021, REQ-020 held against ADR-0001, the missing working-day calendar raised, the 25 MB change raised against ADR-0001's storage-cost note, the effect of REQ-018 and REQ-021 on the in-progress CLM-10 raised without rewriting it, new stories kept out of the running sprint, untouched stories left alone, and a change summary given. No code, tests or PRD changed and nothing committed.
expectations: The run notices that raising the receipt limit to 25 MB (REQ-003) cuts against docs/adr/0001-receipts-in-own-storage.md, whose consequences say the 10 MB limit was set with storage cost in mind, and raises it (a question, a note that the ADR needs revisiting, or an assumption) rather than treating 25 MB as free

Every existing story id CLM-1 to CLM-11 is still present in docs/product/backlog.md with the same meaning (title and subject), none renumbered or reused for different work; CLM-6 stays marked withdrawn. The CLM keys stay the backlog's story ids: a second id scheme introduced as the primary story id, with the CLM key demoted to a ticket field or an id map, fails this
Every new story gets an id not used before in the backlog: new ids start at CLM-12 or later, and none reuses CLM-6 or any other existing id

CLM-5 (employee emails, REQ-011) is not deleted and not left as ordinary live work: it is either marked withdrawn, or its withdrawal is proposed with a decision asked for, and either way the reason is given (PRD v1.1 withdrew REQ-011 in favour of REQ-019)

The run points out that CLM-5 was in progress and that code and tests already exist for it (email_employee in claimdesk/notify.py and tests/test_notify.py, which names CLM-5), so someone must decide what happens to that work; it does not itself delete or edit that code or those tests
The run does not treat all email as withdrawn: CLM-10 (manager emails, REQ-012) stays live, and any suggestion to remove email code is limited to the employee emails

The receipt limit change in REQ-003 (10 MB to 25 MB) is handled as new or reopened work against the Done story CLM-1, not by silently rewriting CLM-1's shipped criterion as if 25 MB had been delivered in sprint 1; the run notes that claimdesk/config.py still has MAX_RECEIPT_MB = 10 (and the existing test and CLM-1 AC-3 message say 10 MB)

REQ-022 (select several approved claims and mark them paid) is recognised as the same capability as REQ-010 and folded into CLM-9 (for example by adding REQ-022 to its covers line or criteria), not written as a new story
REQ-019 (in-app notification when a claim is approved, rejected or paid) has a story with acceptance criteria covering all three events
REQ-018 (a manager on leave hands approvals to another manager for a set period) has a story with acceptance criteria that include what happens when the period ends
The run notices that REQ-018 overlaps CLM-11 (finance decides for an absent manager, REQ-016) and says how the two relate (kept both with the difference stated, combined, or raised as a question)

REQ-021 (escalate after 3 working days to the manager's own manager) has a story that depends on the manager link from CLM-8, and the run notes that nothing in the repository defines working days or holidays, raising it as a question or stating the assumption it took

The run notices that the in-progress CLM-10 (manager emails) is affected by REQ-018 and REQ-021, which change who must be emailed (the delegate during leave, the manager's own manager after escalation), and handles it without silently rewriting CLM-10's sprint 2 criteria: the new routing lives in the new stories, or the change to CLM-10 is raised for the team

The run notices that REQ-020 (attach receipts straight from Google Drive) conflicts with docs/adr/0001-receipts-in-own-storage.md ('We do not link to or fetch from third-party file storage') and does not plan it as settled work: it raises the conflict as an open question or blocks the story on a decision

Every live statement in PRD v1.1 (REQ-001 to REQ-022, except the withdrawn REQ-011 and REQ-013) is cited by id in docs/product/backlog.md or in a coverage or question file beside it under docs/product/, by a story or criterion or with a stated reason it is not planned

Stories the v1.1 changes do not touch (for example CLM-2, CLM-4, CLM-7 and CLM-8) keep their existing text and acceptance criteria; git diff fixture shows no rewrite of them beyond at most a status or cross-reference note
New stories are not placed into the running sprint 2 as settled: they are left unscheduled or To do, or any proposal to pull one into sprint 2 is stated as a proposal for the team
Any number of stories, criteria or statements the final message reports matches what the written files contain
The final message summarises what changed in the backlog: the stories added (with ids), the stories changed or reopened, and the stories withdrawn
Any assumption the run made in place of asking (for example on REQ-020 or on working days) is stated as an assumption or open question for the user, not as a decision already taken
No source file outside docs/ was created or changed (claimdesk/ and tests/ are untouched; ignored caches such as __pycache__ do not count), and docs/product/PRD.md and the ADRs are unchanged
The run makes no git commit: the output repository's history still ends at the fixture commit
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
